## Overview

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that provides 6 tools for image downloading, compression, batch processing, filename synchronization, OCR text extraction, and configuration discovery.

### Quick Start

```bash
npx -y image-processor-mcp
```

### Key Features

- Download images from URLs or search by keyword (Pexels integration)
- Compress and convert single images with 10 output formats
- Recursive compression to target file size
- Lossless and lossy compression with configurable quality and CPU effort
- Auto-resize oversized images
- Batch process entire directories preserving folder structure
- Filename and directory name normalization
- Auto-generated markdown compression reports
- Auto-generated filename mappings paired with reports
- Scan project files and replace old filenames with new ones
- OCR text extraction (100+ languages, runs 100% locally)

---

## Installation & Configuration

### Install from npm

```bash
npm install image-processor-mcp
```

### Requirements

- **Node.js 18** or higher

### MCP Configuration

#### Claude Desktop

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "image-processor-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "image-processor-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY": "your_pexels_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### VS Code (Cline / MCP extensions)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "image-processor-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "image-processor-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY": "your_pexels_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> `IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY` is optional — only needed for keyword search in `download_image`. Get a free key at [https://www.pexels.com/api/key/](https://www.pexels.com/api/key/).

---

## 1. download_image

Downloads an image from a URL or searches by keyword. Optionally compress/convert the image.

### Modes

| Mode | Parameter | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| **URL mode** | `url` | Direct download from an image URL |
| **Search mode** | `query` | Keyword search via Pexels |

If both provided, search mode takes priority.

### Parameters

| `url` | string | no* | — | Direct image URL |
| `query` | string | no* | — | Search keyword |
| `outputPath` | string | yes | — | Save path |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | *original* | `webp`, `avif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `tiff`, `gif` |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | 1–100 |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Lossless mode |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6 |
| `width` | number | no | — | Target width |
| `height` | number | no | — | Target height |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize threshold |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iterative size targeting |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target KB |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `10` | Per-iteration decrease |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality |

*\* One of `url` or `query` is required.*

### Data Flow

```
Request → type guard → Controller
  ├─ Search mode? → Pexels API → first hit URL
  └─ URL mode?    → use directly
  ↓
axios.get(url, arraybuffer, 30s timeout)
  ↓
Write to temp file → check compression params
  ├─ YES → ImageService.compressImage → clean temp → return result
  └─ NO  → move to final path → return success
```

### Response Example (search + compression)

```json
{
  "query": "mountain sunset",
  "imageId": 12345,
  "width": 1920,
  "height": 1080,
  "imageSize": 0,
  "user": "John Doe",
  "tags": "mountain sunset",
  "inputPath": "...",
  "outputPath": "./images/mountain.webp",
  "originalSize": 500000,
  "compressedSize": 80000,
  "compressionRatio": 84.00,
  "success": true,
  "iterations": 1,
  "qualitySteps": [85],
  "finalQuality": 85,
  "exceededTarget": false
}
```

### Edge Cases

- **No url or query**: Error — must provide one
- **Empty search results**: Error — no images found
- **Missing API key**: Error — `IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY` not set
- **Download timeout (30s)**: Error — timeout exceeded
- **Compression fails**: Temp file cleaned up, error returned

---

## 2. compress_image

Compress or convert a single image with full control over quality, dimensions, format, and recursive compression.

### Parameters

| `inputPath` | string | yes | — | Source image path |
| `outputPath` | string | yes | — | Destination path |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | `webp` | Output format |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | 1–100 |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Lossless mode |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6 |
| `width` | number | no | — | Target width |
| `height` | number | no | — | Target height |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize threshold |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iterative targeting |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target KB |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `10` | Per-iteration decrease |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality |

### Core Compression Algorithm

```
1. Read original size + image metadata (sharp)
2. Compute resize:
   - Explicit w/h? → use those
   - Exceeds maxDimension? → scale proportionally
   - Otherwise → no resize
3. Loop:
   - sharp pipeline → apply format with quality
   - If input === output → buffer (safe in-place)
   - Else → write to file
   - If recursive + over target + above floor → reduce quality, loop
   - Else → break
4. Return CompressionResult
```

### Format Conversion

| Format | Sharp Options |
|--------|---------------|
| `webp` | `{quality, lossless, effort, smartSubsample, alphaQuality:90}` |
| `avif` | `{quality, lossless, effort}` |
| `jpeg` | `{quality, mozjpeg:true}` |
| `png` | `{compressionLevel:9}` |
| `tiff` | `{quality, compression:'lzw'}` |
| `gif` | `gif()` (no options) |
| *other* | Falls back to WebP |

### Response Example

```json
{
  "inputPath": "./input/photo.jpg",
  "outputPath": "./output/photo.webp",
  "originalSize": 500000,
  "compressedSize": 80000,
  "compressionRatio": 84.00,
  "success": true,
  "iterations": 1,
  "qualitySteps": [85],
  "finalQuality": 85,
  "exceededTarget": false
}
```

### Edge Cases

- **In-place compression** (same path): Buffer-based to avoid corruption
- **Missing input file**: `success: false` with error
- **Unknown format**: Falls back to WebP
- **Recursion floor**: Stops when quality can't decrease further
- **Abort**: Returns partial result with `success: false`

---

## 3. compress_directory

Batch compress all images in a directory recursively, preserving folder structure. Generates report + mappings.

### Parameters

| `inputDir` | string | yes | — | Source directory |
| `outputDir` | string | yes | — | Output directory |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | `webp` | Output format |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | 1–100 |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Lossless mode |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6 |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize threshold |
| `normalizeFilename` | boolean | no | `false` | Clean filenames |
| `filenameReplaceChars` | string | no | ` , -, ., &` | Replace chars |
| `filenameCase` | string | no | `lowercase` | Case conversion |
| `normalizeDirname` | boolean | no | `false` | Clean dir names |
| `dirnameReplaceChars` | string | no | ` , -, ., &` | Dir replace chars |
| `dirnameCase` | string | no | `lowercase` | Dir case |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iterative targeting |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target KB |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `5` (schema) / `10` (code) | Per-iteration decrease |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality |

### Data Flow

```
Request → type guard → Controller
  ├─ Validate input directory exists
  ├─ Apply defaults, build FileNamingOptions
  ├─ Scan all image files (recursive)
  ├─ Filter out SVG (restricted)
  ├─ For each file:
  │   ├─ Compute output path (preserves structure, normalizes, changes ext)
  │   └─ Run ImageService.compressImage
  ├─ Generate report (.image-processor-mcp/reports/)
  └─ Generate mappings JSON (.image-processor-mcp/mappings/)
```

### Output Path Algorithm

```
relativePath = inputDir → inputFile difference

1. Dir naming enabled → normalize each directory component
2. File naming enabled → normalize basename
3. Replace extension with .{outputFormat}
4. Prepend outputDir
```

### normalizeName

```
Replace each char → '_', collapse multiple '_', trim edges, apply case
```

### Generated Files

```
.image-processor-mcp/
├── reports/scan-report-{timestamp}.md
└── mappings/mappings-{timestamp}.json
```

### Response Example

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "totalFiles": 10,
  "successful": 9,
  "failed": 1,
  "totalOriginalSize": 5000000,
  "totalCompressedSize": 1200000,
  "overallReduction": 76.00,
  "durationMs": 5432,
  "reportPath": ".image-processor-mcp/reports/scan-report-2026-05-29-15-30-00.md",
  "mappingsPath": ".image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-2026-05-29-15-30-00.json"
}
```

### Edge Cases

- **Input dir not found**: Early error, no files written
- **SVG files**: Silently excluded
- **Abort mid-batch**: Partial results processed
- **All files fail**: No mappings file generated
- **No images found**: Empty report

---

## 4. sync_filenames

Scan project files and replace all references to old filenames with new filenames after compression.

### Parameters

| `scanDir` | string | yes | — | Directory to scan |
| `mappingFilePath` | string | no | — | Path to mappings JSON file |
| `mappings` | array | no | — | Inline `{oldFileName, newFileName}[]` |
| `includeExtensions` | array | no | html,js,ts,css,md,json... | Extensions to scan |
| `excludeDirectories` | array | no | node_modules,.git,build,dist... | Dirs to skip |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | `true` | Preview only |

### Validation

When using `mappingFilePath`:
1. File exists + valid JSON
2. Mappings array present and non-empty
3. Each entry has `oldFileName` and `newFileName` (strings)
4. Timestamp extracted from filename `mappings-(.+).json`
5. Matching report must exist: `reports/scan-report-{timestamp}.md`

If the matching report is missing → operation **rejected** (prevents stale mappings).

### Data Flow

```
Request → type guard → Controller
  ├─ mappingFilePath?
  │   YES → ReferenceService.readMappingFile → validate against report
  │   NO  → use inline mappings
  ├─ dryRun = args.dryRun !== false
  ├─ ReferenceService.scanReferences:
  │   ├─ Collect files recursively (filtered by extension, excluding dirs)
  │   ├─ For each file:
  │   │   ├─ For each mapping:
  │   │   │   ├─ Regex-escape oldFileName, count occurrences
  │   │   │   ├─ Build line-by-line details
  │   │   │   ├─ Build preview (3 lines context)
  │   │   │   └─ If !dryRun: replace in content
  │   │   └─ If modified: write file
  │   └─ Return UpdateRefResult
  └─ ReportService.generateSyncReport → .image-processor-mcp/syncs/
```

### Generated Files

```
.image-processor-mcp/syncs/sync-report-{timestamp}.md           (live)
.image-processor-mcp/syncs/dry-run/sync-report-{timestamp}.md   (dry-run)
```

### Response Example

```
Dry run — no files were modified.

Mapping source: .image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-2026-05-29-15-30-00.json
Files scanned: 42
Files with matches: 3
Total replacements: 12

--- Matches ---

[src/components/Header.tsx]
  "logo.png" → "logo.webp" (5x)
  Preview: ... context lines ...
  Line 15:23  "logo.png" → "logo.webp"
  ... and 3 more (see report)

Report saved to: .image-processor-mcp/syncs/dry-run/sync-report-2026-05-29-15-31-00.md
```

### Edge Cases

- **Mapping file not found**: Error with path
- **Invalid JSON**: Parse error
- **No matching report**: Detailed rejection message
- **Neither source provided**: Error explaining options
- **No matches found**: Informational message
- **Regex special chars**: Properly escaped
- **Binary files**: Filtered by extension list

---

## 5. extract_text

Extract visible printed text from images using OCR (tesseract.js). Runs entirely locally.

### Parameters

| `imagePath` | string | yes | — | Path to image file |
| `language` | string | no | `eng` | Language code (use `+` for multiple) |
| `rectangle` | object | no | — | Region `{top, left, width, height}` |
| `outputFormat` | enum | no | `text` | `text`, `blocks`, `hocr`, `tsv` |
| `preprocess` | boolean | no | `true` | Grayscale + auto-rotate |

### Data Flow

```
Request → type guard → OcrController → OcrService.recognize
  ├─ Validate path (exists, not dir, not empty, not SVG)
  ├─ Validate rectangle (positive dimensions)
  ├─ Build sharp pipeline:
  │   ├─ Convert unsupported formats to PNG
  │   └─ Preprocess: grayscale + rotate
  ├─ runOcr:
  │   ├─ Serialized via jobQueue (one at a time)
  │   ├─ getWorker: reuse / reinitialize / create
  │   ├─ worker.recognize()
  │   └─ Recycle worker every 500 jobs
  └─ Return ExtractTextResult
```

### Worker Lifecycle

| State | Action |
|-------|--------|
| Worker exists, same language | Reuse directly |
| Worker exists, different language | `worker.reinitialize(language)` |
| No worker | `createWorker(language, 1, ...)` |
| After 500 jobs | `setImmediate(recycleWorker)` |
| Worker error | errorHandler nulls out reference |
| SIGINT / transport close | `shutdown()` → terminate |

### Supported Input Formats

| Natively supported | Auto-converted to PNG |
|-------------------|----------------------|
| bmp, jpg, jpeg, png | tiff, heic, heif, webp*, gif* |
| pbm, pgm, ppm | and all others |

*\* webp and gif ARE natively supported by tesseract.js, despite the conversion check. The code converts any extension NOT in `OCR_SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS`. Since webp and gif are in that list, they are NOT converted.*

### Limitations

- **Handwritten text**: NOT supported
- **SVG files**: Rejected (vector format)
- **Empty images**: Return empty string (not an error)
- **First run**: Downloads language data (~2MB) from CDN

### Response Example (text format)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "text": "Extracted text content",
  "confidence": 92.5,
  "words": 42,
  "language": "eng",
  "durationMs": 1234,
  "preprocessed": true
}
```

### Edge Cases

- **SVG**: Explicit rejection
- **Unsupported format**: Auto-converted to PNG
- **Worker crash**: Auto-recovery (errorHandler nulls out)
- **Abort**: DOMException caught → cancelled result
- **Empty file (0 bytes)**: Explicit rejection
- **Path is directory**: Explicit rejection

---

## 6. get_acknowledgement

Returns comprehensive documentation of all tools, defaults, formats, and environment variables.

### Parameters

**None** — empty input schema.

### Response

A full markdown document built dynamically from all configuration constants:

| Section | Source |
|---------|--------|
| All 6 tools | Hardcoded descriptions |
| Configuration defaults | `DEFAULTS` + `CONFIG_DESCRIPTIONS` |
| Supported input formats | `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` + `INPUT_EXTENSION_DESCRIPTIONS` |
| Supported output formats | `SUPPORTED_OUTPUT_FORMATS` + `OUTPUT_FORMAT_DESCRIPTIONS` |
| Sync scan defaults | `DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS` + `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DIRS` |
| Restricted extensions | `RESTRICTED_EXTENSIONS` |
| Environment variables | Hardcoded |
| Credits | Hardcoded |

### Implementation

```ts
ToolController.handleGetAcknowledgement()
  // Synchronous — no abort signal, no async
  // Returns { content: [{ type: 'text', text: markdown }] }
```

### Edge Cases

None — always succeeds, no parameters, no I/O.

---

## Configuration Defaults

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `quality` | `85` | Compression quality for lossy formats (1–100) |
| `lossless` | `false` | Lossless compression (WebP, PNG, GIF, AVIF) |
| `effort` | `6` | CPU effort (0–6). Higher = smaller files |
| `maxDimension` | `2000` | Auto-resize threshold in pixels |
| `expectedSizeKB` | `100` | Target file size for recursive compression |
| `qualityStepDown` | `10` | Quality decrease per recursive iteration |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | `10` | Minimum quality (1–100) during recursion |
| `outputFormat` | `webp` | Default output format |
| `filenameCase` | `lowercase` | Filename case conversion |
| `dirnameCase` | `lowercase` | Directory name case conversion |
| `filenameReplaceChars` | `[' ', '-', '.', '&']` | Characters replaced with `_` in filenames |
| `dirnameReplaceChars` | `[' ', '-', '.', '&']` | Characters replaced with `_` in dir names |

## Supported Formats

### Input Formats (35+)

`.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.bmp`, `.tiff`, `.tif`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.svg`, `.heic`, `.heif`, `.ico`, `.cur`, `.jp2`, `.j2k`, `.jpf`, `.jpx`, `.jpm`, `.mj2`, `.jxr`, `.wdp`, `.hdp`, `.psd`, `.psb`, `.dds`, `.tga`, `.vda`, `.icb`, `.vst`, `.pbm`, `.pgm`, `.ppm`, `.pnm`, `.pfm`, `.exr`, `.hdr`, `.hrd`, `.pic`, `.pict`, `.pct`, `.xbm`, `.xpm`, `.wal`, `.cut`, `.ras`, `.sun`, `.sgi`, `.rgb`, `.rgba`, `.bw`, `.pcx`, `.pcd`, `.iff`, `.lbm`

### Output Formats (10)

| Format | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `webp` | Google WebP. Excellent lossy/lossless. Supports transparency. |
| `avif` | AV1-based. 30–50% smaller than JPEG. Slower encoding. |
| `jpeg` | Universal compatibility. No transparency. |
| `png` | Lossless with transparency. Best for graphics/logos. |
| `tiff` | High-quality. Print/publishing. Largest sizes. |
| `gif` | Animation + transparency. 256 colors. |
| `heif` | HEVC-based. Apple ecosystem. |
| `jp2` | JPEG 2000. Wavelet-based. Medical/ cinema. |
| `jxl` | JPEG XL. Next-gen. Lossless JPEG re-encoding. |
| `pdf` | Convert images to PDF pages. |

### Restricted Extensions

`.svg` — SVG files are skipped during batch compression (vector format — sharp cannot safely compress without breaking rendering).

# download_image

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/01-download-image.md

# download_image

Downloads an image from a URL or searches by keyword. Optionally compress/convert the image in a single step.

## Modes

| Mode | Parameter | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| **URL mode** | `url` | Direct download from an image URL |
| **Search mode** | `query` | Keyword search via Pexels (requires `IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY`) |

If both `url` and `query` are provided, search mode takes priority.

## Parameters

| `url` | string | no* | — | Direct URL to an image. Required if `query` is not provided. |
| `query` | string | no* | — | Search keyword to find an image. Required if `url` is not provided. |
| `outputPath` | string | yes | — | Filesystem path where the image will be saved. |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | *original* | Output format. Supported: `webp`, `avif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `tiff`, `gif`. |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | Compression quality 1–100. Higher = more detail. |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Use lossless compression (WebP, PNG, GIF, AVIF only). |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6. Higher = smaller files but slower. |
| `width` | number | no | — | Exact target width in pixels. Aspect ratio maintained if height is not set. |
| `height` | number | no | — | Exact target height in pixels. Aspect ratio maintained if width is not set. |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize if width or height exceeds this threshold. |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iteratively reduce quality until file is under `expectedSizeKB`. |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target file size in KB for recursive compression. |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `10` | Quality decrease per recursive iteration. |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality (1–100) allowed during recursive compression. |

## Internal Data Flow

```
Request
  ↓
index.ts — type guard (isDownloadImageArgs)
  ↓
ToolController.handleDownloadImage()
  ├─ hasQuery? → SearchService.searchImages() [Pexels API]
  │               └─ picks first hit → imageUrl, sourceInfo
  └─ hasUrl?   → uses url directly
  ↓
axios.get(imageUrl, { responseType: 'arraybuffer', timeout: 30000 })
  ↓
Write to temp file: {dirname}/.temp_{basename}
  ↓
hasCompressParams?
  ├─ YES → ImageService.compressImage(tempPath, outputPath, options)
  │         └─ fs.remove(tempPath)
  │         └─ Return JSON: {sourceInfo + CompressionResult}
  └─ NO  → fs.move(tempPath → outputPath)
            └─ Return JSON: {success, outputPath, fileSize}
```

## Edge Cases

- **No url or query**: Returns error — "You must provide either a 'url' to download directly, or a 'query' to search for an image."
- **Empty search results**: Returns error — "No images found for query: ..."
- **Missing API key**: `SearchService.getClient()` throws — "IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY environment variable is not set."
- **Download timeout** (30s): axios throws — handled as "Failed to download image: timeout"
- **Compression fails**: Temp file cleaned up silently `.catch(() => {})`, error returned with full `CompressionResult`
- **Both url and query**: Search mode wins

## Response Example (Search + Compression)

```json
{
  "query": "mountain sunset",
  "imageId": 12345,
  "width": 1920,
  "height": 1080,
  "imageSize": 0,
  "user": "John Doe",
  "tags": "mountain sunset landscape",
  "inputPath": "...",
  "outputPath": "./images/mountain.webp",
  "originalSize": 500000,
  "compressedSize": 80000,
  "compressionRatio": 84.00,
  "success": true,
  "iterations": 1,
  "qualitySteps": [85],
  "finalQuality": 85,
  "exceededTarget": false
}
```

## Response Example (URL only, no compression)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "outputPath": "./images/photo.jpg",
  "fileSize": 500000
}
```

---

# compress_image

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/02-compress-image.md

# compress_image

Compress or convert a single image with format conversion, quality adjustment, resizing, and optional recursive compression.

## Parameters

| `inputPath` | string | yes | — | Path to the source image file. |
| `outputPath` | string | yes | — | Path where the compressed image will be saved. |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | `webp` | Output format. Supported: `webp`, `avif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `tiff`, `gif`. |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | Compression quality 1–100. |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Use lossless compression (WebP, PNG, GIF, AVIF only). |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6. Higher = smaller files but slower. |
| `width` | number | no | — | Exact target width in pixels. |
| `height` | number | no | — | Exact target height in pixels. |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize if width or height exceeds this threshold. |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iteratively reduce quality until target size is met. |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target file size for recursive compression (KB). |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `10` | Quality reduction per recursive iteration. |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality (1–100) allowed during recursion. |

## Internal Data Flow

```
Request
  ↓
index.ts — type guard (isCompressImageArgs)
  ↓
ToolController.handleCompressImage()
  ├─ FileService.ensureDir(path.dirname(outputPath))
  └─ ImageService.compressImage(inputPath, outputPath, options, signal)
       ↓
       Core compression engine (shared with download_image & compress_directory)
```

## ImageService.compressImage — Core Algorithm

```
1. Read originalSize (FileService.getFileSize)
2. Read metadata via sharp(inputPath).metadata() → imgWidth, imgHeight
3. Compute resizeOptions:
   - Explicit width/height given? → use those
   - Image exceeds maxDimension? → scale proportionally (fit: 'inside', withoutEnlargement: true)
   - Otherwise → no resize
4. Recursive loop:
   while (true):
     check abort signal
     pipeline = sharp(inputPath)
     apply resize if needed
     pipeline = applyFormat(pipeline, format, {quality, lossless, effort})
     if inputPath === outputPath → toBuffer() + fs.writeFile (in-place safe)
     else → toFile(outputPath)
     check compressedSize
     if recursiveCompress AND over target AND above floor → reduce quality, loop
     else → break
5. Return CompressionResult
```

## applyFormat — Format Conversion Matrix

| Format | Sharp Options | Notes |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| `webp` | `{quality, lossless, effort, smartSubsample: true, alphaQuality: 90}` | Best all-around |
| `avif` | `{quality, lossless, effort}` | Best compression, slowest |
| `jpeg` | `{quality, mozjpeg: true}` | Universal compatibility |
| `png` | `{compressionLevel: 9}` | Lossless only, ignores quality/effort |
| `tiff` | `{quality, compression: 'lzw'}` | Print/publishing |
| `gif` | `gif()` (no options) | 256-color limit |
| `default` | `webp({quality, lossless})` | Falls back to WebP |

## Edge Cases

- **In-place compression** (inputPath === outputPath): Uses buffer to avoid corrupting the original
- **Input file missing**: `sharp(inputPath).metadata()` throws → `success: false` with error message
- **Unsupported format** (heif, jp2, jxl, pdf): Silently falls back to WebP
- **Recursive compression floor**: Loop stops when `currentQuality - qualityStepDown < minimumQualityFloor`
- **Abort mid-recursion**: Returns partial result with `success: false, error: 'Operation cancelled'`

## Response Example

```json
{
  "inputPath": "./input/photo.jpg",
  "outputPath": "./output/photo.webp",
  "originalSize": 500000,
  "compressedSize": 80000,
  "compressionRatio": 84.00,
  "success": true,
  "iterations": 1,
  "qualitySteps": [85],
  "finalQuality": 85,
  "exceededTarget": false
}
```

---

# compress_directory

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/03-compress-directory.md

# compress_directory

Batch compress all images in a directory recursively, preserving folder structure. Generates a detailed markdown report and optional filename mappings JSON for use with `sync_filenames`.

## Parameters

| `inputDir` | string | yes | — | Root directory containing images to compress. |
| `outputDir` | string | yes | — | Root directory where compressed images will be saved (mirrors input structure). |
| `outputFormat` | string | no | `webp` | Output format for all images. |
| `quality` | number | no | `85` | Compression quality 1–100. |
| `lossless` | boolean | no | `false` | Use lossless compression (WebP, PNG, GIF, AVIF). |
| `effort` | number | no | `6` | CPU effort 0–6. Higher = smaller but slower. |
| `maxDimension` | number | no | `2000` | Auto-resize threshold in pixels. |
| `normalizeFilename` | boolean | no | `false` | Enable filename normalization (replace chars, apply case). |
| `filenameReplaceChars` | string | no | ` , -, ., &` | Characters to replace with underscore (comma-separated). |
| `filenameCase` | string | no | `lowercase` | `lowercase`, `uppercase`, or `original`. |
| `normalizeDirname` | boolean | no | `false` | Enable directory name normalization. |
| `dirnameReplaceChars` | string | no | ` , -, ., &` | Characters to replace in directory names (comma-separated). |
| `dirnameCase` | string | no | `lowercase` | `lowercase`, `uppercase`, or `original`. |
| `recursiveCompress` | boolean | no | `false` | Iteratively reduce oversized outputs. |
| `expectedSizeKB` | number | no | `100` | Target file size in KB. |
| `qualityStepDown` | number | no | `5`* | Quality decrease per iteration. |
| `minimumQualityFloor` | number | no | `10` | Minimum quality allowed (1–100). |

> **Note**: The input schema states `qualityStepDown` default is `5`, but the controller applies `DEFAULTS.qualityStepDown` which is `10`. The actual behavior uses `10`.

## Internal Data Flow

```
Request
  ↓
index.ts — type guard (isCompressDirectoryArgs)
  ↓
ToolController.handleCompressDirectory()
  ├─ path.resolve(inputDir), path.resolve(outputDir)
  ├─ fs.pathExists(inputDir) — error if not found
  ├─ FileService.ensureDir(outputDir)
  ├─ Apply defaults (?? operator for most, || for outputFormat)
  ├─ Build FileNamingOptions (file + dir naming)
  │
  ├─ FileService.getImageFiles(inputDir) — recursive scan
  │   └─ Filter out RESTRICTED_EXTENSIONS ['.svg']
  │
  ├─ For each image file (sequential):
  │   ├─ Check abort signal
  │   ├─ FileService.getOutputPath(inputPath, inputDir, outputDir, format, fileNaming, dirNaming)
  │   │   └─ preserves relative structure, applies normalization, changes extension
  │   ├─ FileService.ensureDir(dirname(outputPath))
  │   └─ ImageService.compressImage(inputPath, outputPath, options, signal)
  │       └─ Push result to results[]
  │
  ├─ ReportService.generateReport(results, inputDir, outputDir, format, startTime, duration)
  │   └─ Output: .image-processor-mcp/reports/scan-report-{timestamp}.md
  │
  ├─ Generate mappings JSON (if successful.length > 0):
  │   └─ Output: .image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-{timestamp}.json
  │
  └─ Return summary JSON
```

## getOutputPath — Path Mapping Algorithm

```
Input: inputPath, inputDir, outputDir, format, fileNaming, dirNaming

1. relativePath = path.relative(inputDir, inputPath)
   e.g. subdir/photo.png

2. If dirNaming.enabled:
   - normalize each directory component (replace chars, case)
   - reassemble with filename

3. If fileNaming.enabled:
   - strip extension from basename
   - normalize basename (replace chars, case)
   - reassemble

4. Replace extension: .{format}

5. Prepend outputDir
```

## normalizeName Algorithm

```
1. For each char in replaceChars: split(char).join('_')
2. Collapse consecutive underscores: /_+/g → '_'
3. Trim leading/trailing underscores: /^_|_$/g
4. Apply case: toLowerCase() or toUpperCase()
```

## Generated Report Structure

**Path**: `.image-processor-mcp/reports/scan-report-{YYYY-MM-DD-HH-mm-ss}.md`

**Sections**:
1. **Header** — server name, version, generation time, duration
2. **Summary** — total files, successful, failed, sizes, reduction %
3. **File Tree** — ASCII directory tree of output (directories first, then files, alphabetically)
4. **File Details** — per-file: input size, output size, compression ratio, iterations
5. **Failed Files** — list of errors (if any)
6. **Input vs Output Comparison** — table with status
7. **Skipped Files Notice** — currently unused (skippedFiles defaults to [])
8. **Footer** — credits

## Generated Mappings JSON

**Path**: `.image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-{same-timestamp}.json`

```json
{
  "generatedAt": "2026-05-29T15:30:00.000Z",
  "tool": "compress_directory",
  "mappings": [
    { "oldFileName": "photo.png", "newFileName": "photo.webp" },
    { "oldFileName": "banner.jpg", "newFileName": "banner.avif" }
  ]
}
```

**Only generated if**: timestamp is extractable from report filename AND at least one successful compression.

## Response Example

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "totalFiles": 10,
  "successful": 9,
  "failed": 1,
  "totalOriginalSize": 5000000,
  "totalCompressedSize": 1200000,
  "overallReduction": 76.00,
  "durationMs": 5432,
  "reportPath": ".image-processor-mcp/reports/scan-report-2026-05-29-15-30-00.md",
  "mappingsPath": ".image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-2026-05-29-15-30-00.json"
}
```

## Edge Cases

- **Input directory not found**: Early return with error, no files written
- **SVG files**: Silently excluded (filtered via `RESTRICTED_EXTENSIONS`), no warning in response
- **Abort mid-batch**: Partial results processed, report + mappings generated for what completed
- **All files fail**: `successful: 0`, mappings file NOT generated
- **No image files found**: Empty report generated (no file tree, no details)
- **Normalization disabled**: Direct pass-through of relative paths

# sync_filenames

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/04-sync-filenames.md

# sync_filenames

Scan project source files and replace all references to old filenames with new filenames after compression. Supports file-based mappings (from `compress_directory`) and inline LLM-provided mappings.

## Parameters

| `scanDir` | string | yes | — | Root directory to scan for files containing old filename references. |
| `mappingFilePath` | string | no | — | Path to a `mappings-{timestamp}.json` file from `compress_directory`. |
| `mappings` | array | no | — | Inline array of `{oldFileName, newFileName}` objects (fallback). |
| `includeExtensions` | array | no | `['.html','.js','.ts','.css','.md',...]` | File extensions to scan. |
| `excludeDirectories` | array | no | `['node_modules','.git','build','dist',...]` | Directories to skip. |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | `true` | Preview only. Set to `false` to apply changes. |

### Mapping Sources

**File-based (recommended)**:
```json
{
  "scanDir": "./src",
  "mappingFilePath": ".image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-2026-05-29-15-30-00.json",
  "dryRun": true
}
```

**Inline (fallback)**:
```json
{
  "scanDir": "./src",
  "mappings": [
    { "oldFileName": "logo.png", "newFileName": "logo.webp" },
    { "oldFileName": "banner.jpg", "newFileName": "banner.avif" }
  ],
  "dryRun": true
}
```

## Validation Logic

When `mappingFilePath` is provided, the tool:

1. Reads the JSON file and validates its structure
2. Extracts the timestamp from the filename via regex: `/^mappings-(.+)\.json$/`
3. Checks that a matching report exists: `.image-processor-mcp/reports/scan-report-{timestamp}.md`
4. If the matching report does **not** exist → operation is **rejected** with a detailed error

This prevents stale, mismatched, or manually-created mappings from being applied.

## Internal Data Flow

```
Request
  ↓
index.ts — type guard (isUpdateReferencesArgs)
  └─ Requires: scanDir AND (mappingFilePath OR valid mappings array)
  ↓
ToolController.handleUpdateReferences()
  ├─ mappingFilePath provided?
  │   YES → ReferenceService.readMappingFile(path)
  │          ├─ Validate file exists
  │          ├─ Parse JSON, validate structure
  │          ├─ Extract timestamp from filename
  │          ├─ Validate matching report exists
  │          └─ Return mappings + timestamp
  │   NO → use args.mappings array directly
  │
  ├─ dryRun = args.dryRun !== false
  │
  ├─ ReferenceService.scanReferences(scanDir, mappings, dryRun, includeExtensions, excludeDirs, signal)
  │   ├─ Resolve + validate scanDir
  │   ├─ Normalize extensions (ensure leading '.', lowercase)
  │   ├─ Recursively collect matching files (skip exclude dirs)
  │   ├─ For each file:
  │   │   ├─ Read entire content
  │   │   ├─ For each mapping:
  │   │   │   ├─ Escape regex special chars in oldFileName
  │   │   │   ├─ Count occurrences
  │   │   │   ├─ Build lineDetails (line:column per match)
  │   │   │   ├─ Build preview (3 lines of context before/after)
  │   │   │   ├─ Push ReferenceMatch
  │   │   │   └─ If !dryRun: content = content.replace(regex, newFileName)
  │   │   └─ If modified && !dryRun: fs.writeFile
  │   └─ Return UpdateRefResult
  │
  └─ ReportService.generateSyncReport(result, scanDir)
      └─ Output: .image-processor-mcp/syncs/{dry-run/}sync-report-{timestamp}.md
```

## Reference Match Tracking

Each match captures:
- `lineNumber`: 1-indexed line in the file
- `column`: character index within the line
- `oldValue`: the original filename string
- `newValue`: the replacement filename string

A preview with 3 lines of context on each side is also captured.

## Generated Sync Report

**Path**:
- Dry run: `.image-processor-mcp/syncs/dry-run/sync-report-{timestamp}.md`
- Live: `.image-processor-mcp/syncs/sync-report-{timestamp}.md`

**Sections**:
1. **Header** — server name, version, generation time
2. **Mode** — Dry Run or Live Update
3. **Summary** — files scanned, files with matches, total replacements
4. **Per-file** — each matching file: replacements, preview, line-level details table
5. **Footer** — credits

Also ensures `.image-processor-mcp/README.md` exists (auto-generated directory documentation).

## Response Example

```
Dry run — no files were modified.

Mapping source: .image-processor-mcp/mappings/mappings-2026-05-29-15-30-00.json
Files scanned: 42
Files with matches: 3
Total replacements: 12

--- Matches ---

[src/components/Header.tsx]
  "logo.png" → "logo.webp" (5x)
  Preview: ... context lines ...
  Line 15:23  "logo.png" → "logo.webp"
  Line 42:8  "logo.png" → "logo.webp"
  ... and 3 more (see report)

Report saved to: .image-processor-mcp/syncs/dry-run/sync-report-2026-05-29-15-31-00.md
```

## Edge Cases

- **Mapping file not found**: `readMappingFile` throws → "Failed to update references: Mapping file not found"
- **Invalid JSON in mapping file**: Throws → "Invalid JSON in mapping file"
- **Empty mappings in file**: Throws → "Mapping file has no valid mappings array"
- **No matching report for timestamp**: Returns error with instructions
- **Neither source provided**: Returns error explaining both options
- **scanDir doesn't exist**: `scanReferences` throws → caught
- **No matches found**: Response says "No references to any of the specified filenames were found."
- **Regex special chars**: Properly escaped — safe for any filename
- **Binary files**: Filtered by includeExtensions (only text-based extensions scanned)

---

# extract_text

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/05-extract-text.md

# extract_text

Extract visible printed text from images using OCR (tesseract.js). Runs entirely locally — no API keys, no cloud calls, no data leaves your machine.

## Parameters

| `imagePath` | string | yes | — | Path to the image file. |
| `language` | string | no | `eng` | Language code. Use `+` for multiple languages, e.g. `"eng+chi_sim"`. |
| `rectangle` | object | no | — | Restrict OCR to a specific region: `{top, left, width, height}`. |
| `outputFormat` | enum | no | `text` | Output format: `text`, `blocks` (JSON with positions), `hocr` (HTML-like), `tsv` (tab-separated). |
| `preprocess` | boolean | no | `true` | Auto-preprocess: grayscale + auto-rotate + resolution normalization. |

## Internal Data Flow

```
Request
  ↓
index.ts — type guard (isExtractTextArgs)
  ↓
OcrController.handleExtractText()
  ↓
OcrService.recognize(args, signal)
  ├─ Abort check
  ├─ Apply defaults: language='eng', outputFormat='text', preprocess=true
  ├─ Validate outputFormat ∈ ['text', 'blocks', 'hocr', 'tsv']
  │
  ├─ Path validation:
  │   ├─ fs.pathExists — fail "Image not found"
  │   ├─ fs.stat — fail if directory
  │   ├─ stat.size === 0 — fail "empty file"
  │   └─ ext === '.svg' — fail "vector format"
  │
  ├─ Rectangle validation (if provided):
  │   ├─ width/height <= 0 → fail
  │   └─ any negative coordinate → fail
  │
  ├─ Build sharp pipeline:
  │   ├─ sharp(imagePath)
  │   ├─ If ext not in OCR_SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS → pipeline.png()
  │   ├─ If preprocess → pipeline.grayscale().rotate()
  │   └─ toBuffer()
  │
  ├─ runOcr(buffer, language, outputFormat, rectangle, signal):
  │   ├─ jobQueue.then(...) — serialized, one job at a time
  │   ├─ getWorker(language):
  │   │   ├─ Worker exists + same language? → reuse
  │   │   ├─ Worker exists + different language? → worker.reinitialize()
  │   │   └─ No worker? → createWorker(language, 1, {cacheMethod:'none', errorHandler})
  │   ├─ worker.recognize(buffer, {rectangle?}, {text:true, blocks?, hocr?, tsv?})
  │   ├─ jobCount++; if >= 500 → setImmediate(recycleWorker)
  │   └─ Return result
  │
  ├─ Compute duration, word count
  ├─ Build ExtractTextResult (conditionally attach blocks/hocr/tsv)
  └─ Return result
```

## Worker Lifecycle

The `OcrService` manages a single cached tesseract.js worker:

```
Static state:
  worker: Worker | null
  currentLanguage: string | null
  jobCount: number
  jobQueue: Promise (serializer)

Worker reuse:
  - Same language → reuse directly (fast path)
  - Different language → worker.reinitialize(language)
  - Worker died → errorHandler nulls out, next call creates new

Worker recycling (after 500 jobs):
  - setImmediate → worker.terminate() → worker = null
  - Prevents memory bloat over long usage

Shutdown:
  - Called on SIGINT and transport close
  - Gracefully terminates worker
```

## Supported Input Formats for OCR

| Format | Native | Fallback |
|--------|--------|----------|
| `.bmp`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png` | ✓ Direct | — |
| `.pbm`, `.pgm`, `.ppm` | ✓ Direct | — |
| `.webp`, `.gif` | ✓ Direct | — |
| `.tiff`, `.tif`, `.heic`, `.heif`, etc. | ✗ | Auto-converted to PNG via sharp |

## Output Formats

| Format | Description | Response Field |
|--------|-------------|----------------|
| `text` | Plain extracted text (default) | `text` |
| `blocks` | JSON with per-word positions, confidence, bounding boxes | `blocks` |
| `hocr` | HTML-like structured markup | `hocr` |
| `tsv` | Tab-separated values table | `tsv` |

## Limitations

- **Handwritten text**: NOT supported. Tesseract OCR is built for printed text only.
- **SVG files**: Rejected — vector format with no raster pixels.
- **Empty results**: Images without printed text return an empty string (not an error).
- **First run**: Downloads language data (~2MB for English) from CDN, then caches locally.

## Response Example

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "text": "Extracted text content here...",
  "confidence": 92.5,
  "words": 42,
  "language": "eng",
  "durationMs": 1234,
  "preprocessed": true
}
```

With `rectangle`:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "text": "Region-specific text",
  "confidence": 88.3,
  "words": 12,
  "language": "eng",
  "durationMs": 890,
  "preprocessed": true,
  "rectangle": { "top": 50, "left": 0, "width": 400, "height": 150 },
  "blocks": [ ... ]
}
```

## Edge Cases

- **SVG file**: Explicit error — "SVG is a vector format with no raster pixels to OCR"
- **Unsupported format** (TIFF, HEIC): Auto-converted to PNG before OCR
- **Rectangle out of bounds**: Passed through to tesseract.js (no explicit image dimension check)
- **Worker error during recognition**: errorHandler nulls out worker; next call creates fresh
- **Abort during OCR**: DOMException caught → `cancelledResult()` returned
- **Empty file** (0 bytes): Explicit rejection before sharp pipeline
- **Path is directory**: Explicit rejection with helpful message

# get_acknowledgement

Source: https://github.com/pansuriyadhvanil/image-processor-mcp/blob/main/docs/06-get-acknowledgement.md

# get_acknowledgement

Returns comprehensive documentation covering all tools, configuration defaults, supported formats, environment variables, and credits. Use this tool as a complete reference for what the MCP server can do.

## Parameters

**None.** Empty input schema — no arguments required.

## Response

Returns a full markdown document as `text` type content (not JSON). The document is built dynamically from all configuration constants.

## Document Sections

1. **Header** — server name, version, author
2. **Tools Overview** — list of all 6 tools
3. **download_image** — full parameter list, modes, workflow, examples
4. **compress_image** — full parameter list, workflow
5. **compress_directory** — full parameter list, workflow, SVG skip notice
6. **sync_filenames** — full parameter list, workflow, validation rules
7. **extract_text** — full parameter list, workflow, limitations, examples
8. **get_acknowledgement** — self-reference
9. **Configuration Defaults** — table of all parameters with defaults and descriptions
10. **Supported Input Formats** — count and overview of all 35+ formats
11. **Supported Output Formats** — 10 formats with descriptions
12. **Sync Scan Defaults** — includeExtensions and excludeDirectories
13. **Restricted Extensions** — SVG
14. **Environment Variables** — IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY
15. **Credits** — Pexels, sharp, tesseract.js, axios, MCP SDK
16. **Repository link**

## Internal Implementation

```ts
ToolController.handleGetAcknowledgement()
  └─ Synchronous — no abort signal, no async operations
  └─ Builds markdown string via template literals
  └─ Interpolates values from:
      ├─ DEFAULTS (all default values)
      ├─ CONFIG_DESCRIPTIONS (parameter descriptions)
      ├─ SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS (input format list)
      ├─ INPUT_EXTENSION_DESCRIPTIONS (format descriptions)
      ├─ SUPPORTED_OUTPUT_FORMATS (output format list)
      ├─ OUTPUT_FORMAT_DESCRIPTIONS (output format descriptions)
      ├─ RESTRICTED_EXTENSIONS (SVG)
      ├─ DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS (sync scan extensions)
      ├─ DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DIRS (sync scan exclude dirs)
      └─ APP_CONFIG (name, version)
```

## Response Format

```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "<full markdown documentation>" }]
}
```

## Example Usage

```json
{
  "tool": "get_acknowledgement",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

## Edge Cases

- **None**: This tool has no parameters, no validation, no async operations, no file I/O. Always succeeds.

## Installation

### From npm

```bash
npm install image-processor-mcp
```

### Requirements

- **Node.js 18** or higher
- **NPM** or compatible package manager

---

## MCP Server Configuration

### What is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows AI assistants (like Claude, Cursor, VS Code extensions, etc.) to connect to external tools and services. This package is an MCP server that exposes image processing capabilities as tools.

### Configuration for Different MCP Hosts

#### Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json)

Add to your `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "image-processor-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "image-processor-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY": "your_pexels_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Note**: The `IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY` is optional — only needed if you want to use the keyword-based image search feature in `download_image`. Get a free API key at [https://www.pexels.com/api/key/](https://www.pexels.com/api/key/).

#### VS Code (via Cline or similar MCP extensions)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "image-processor-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "image-processor-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY": "your_pexels_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Running Directly

```bash
npx -y image-processor-mcp
```

This starts the MCP server on stdio. The server will output diagnostic messages to stderr and communicate with the MCP client via stdin/stdout.

---

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `IMAGE_SEARCH_API_KEY` | No (for search) | Pexels API key for keyword-based image search in `download_image`. Get a free key at [https://www.pexels.com/api/key/](https://www.pexels.com/api/key/). |

---

## Data Directory

All auto-generated files are stored in `.image-processor-mcp/` at the project root:

```
.image-processor-mcp/
├── README.md                          (auto-generated directory guide)
├── reports/
│   └── scan-report-{timestamp}.md     (compression report from compress_directory)
├── mappings/
│   └── mappings-{timestamp}.json      (filename mappings paired with report)
└── syncs/
    ├── sync-report-{timestamp}.md     (live sync results from sync_filenames)
    └── dry-run/
        └── sync-report-{timestamp}.md (dry-run sync results)
```

---

## Technology Stack

| Technology | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| **[Model Context Protocol SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk)** | MCP server framework |
| **[sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/)** | High-performance image processing |
| **[tesseract.js](https://github.com/naptha/tesseract.js/)** | OCR text extraction (100% local) |
| **[Pexels API](https://www.pexels.com/api/)** | Free stock photo search |
| **[axios](https://axios-http.com/)** | HTTP client for downloads |
| **[fs-extra](https://github.com/jprichardson/node-fs-extra)** | Extended file system operations |
| **[dotenv](https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv)** | Environment variable management |
